answer: At the network’s harbor, each agent must stake a verifiable compute token that is released only after a river‑flow of activity proofs are submitted across successive epochs; the vesting schedule rises like a summit, granting incremental reward portions only when the prior proof chain is intact. A sybil farm can generate many identities, but each must immediately lock its own token and endure the same timed proof cadence, so the attacker’s upfront capital equals the sum of all stakes plus the cost of producing valid proofs for every epoch.
